meta.note: This is the single source of truth for all implementation tickets. Epics are feature-based (BE/FE agnostic). Tickets are typed backend or frontend and should be worked on in dependency order within each epic.

frontend.shadcn_mcp: The shadcn MCP tool is installed in this workspace (VS Code). When working on any frontend ticket that involves shadcn/ui components, you can use the MCP tool to: browse available components, fetch component source and usage examples, and get the correct CLI add command. Prefer referencing the MCP tool over copying from external docs — it reflects the exact registry version configured for this project.

definitionOfDone: All acceptance criteria are met and verified manually
A pull request is opened, self-reviewed, and approved by at least one peer
TypeScript compiles with zero errors in strict mode — no `any` without an inline justification comment
All new business logic has unit tests; all new REST endpoints have integration tests
Tests pass locally and in CI before merge
No console.log statements — use NestJS Logger (BE) or a logger utility (FE)
New environment variables are documented in the relevant .env.example
PR description explains the 'why', not just the 'what'
UI changes include a screenshot or short screen recording in the PR
codeQuality: Functions must be single-purpose and under 50 lines; files under 300 lines
No magic strings or numbers — use constants, enums, or named variables
All async operations handle errors explicitly (try/catch or .catch())
State must never be mutated directly — use spreads, structuredClone, or Immer
DTOs must be used for all incoming data (BE: class-validator; FE: Zod or manual validation)
Prefer explicit types over type inference for function signatures and exported values
Avoid deep nesting — extract to named functions if nesting exceeds 3 levels
No commented-out code in merged PRs
testingStandards: Every new function with business logic must have at least: 1 happy-path test, 1 edge-case test, 1 error/invalid-input test
Game engine module (EP-004) has a hard target of 90%+ line coverage
Tests must not depend on execution order — each test is independently runnable
No skipped tests (xit, xdescribe, test.skip) without a comment explaining why
Mocks and stubs must be reset/cleared between tests
Integration tests must use a real test database (not mocked repositories)
Frontend component tests use React Testing Library — no direct enzyme or implementation testing
prStandards: Maximum 400 lines changed per PR — split larger changes into stacked PRs
PR must reference the ticket ID in the title: e.g. '[T-023] Build ProtectedRoute component'
Rebase on main before requesting review — no merge commits
Reviewer should check: correctness, types, tests, edge cases, naming clarity

epics.title: Infrastructure & Project Setup
epics.description: Establish the complete development foundation for both backend and frontend. Neither BE nor FE feature work should begin until this epic is fully done. Covers tooling, database connectivity, local dev environment, CI, and project structure.

tickets.title: Create NestJS module shell structure
tickets.description: Create the empty NestJS module shells for: AuthModule, PlayerModule, MatchModule, GameModule, GameEngineModule, GatewayModule. Each gets a *.module.ts, *.service.ts, and (where applicable) *.controller.ts file with correct decorators. No logic yet — just wiring and DI registration.
acceptanceCriteria: All 6 modules exist under correct src/ subdirectories
Each module is registered in AppModule
pnpm start:dev boots without errors
TypeScript compiles cleanly

tickets.title: Set up Docker Compose with Postgres and Redis
tickets.description: Create docker-compose.yml at the backend root with postgres:16 and redis:7 services, named volumes, correct port mappings (5432, 6379), and environment variable placeholders. Add a .env.example with DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, PORT, NODE_ENV, SESSION_SECRET.
acceptanceCriteria: docker-compose up -d starts both services without errors
Postgres is reachable at localhost:5432
Redis is reachable at localhost:6379
.env.example lists all required variables with placeholder values
.env is in .gitignore

tickets.title: Configure Prisma + PostgreSQL connection
tickets.description: Install Prisma, initialise the schema, configure the DATABASE_URL from @nestjs/config, and wire PrismaService into the app. Create the initial schema.prisma with all tables from the system design: players, matches, match_players, games, game_rankings, game_events. Run the first migration.
acceptanceCriteria: PrismaService is injectable and connects to the local Postgres instance
pnpm prisma migrate dev creates all tables successfully
All columns and foreign keys match the schema in SYSTEM_DESIGN.md §7
PrismaService is globally available (registered as global module)

tickets.title: Configure Redis module with ioredis
tickets.description: Install ioredis, create a RedisModule that reads REDIS_URL from config and exposes an REDIS_CLIENT injection token. Add a startup connectivity check that logs a warning on failure. Register in AppModule.
acceptanceCriteria: REDIS_CLIENT can be injected into any service
App starts and logs 'Redis connected' on successful connection
App starts (with a warning) even if Redis is temporarily unavailable
Connection details come from env — no hardcoded localhost

tickets.title: Add health check endpoint
tickets.description: Install @nestjs/terminus and create GET /health that checks and returns status of: HTTP server, Postgres (via PrismaService.$queryRaw), and Redis (ping). Response shape: { status: 'ok'|'error', components: { postgres: bool, redis: bool } }.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /health returns 200 with { status: 'ok' } when all services are up
GET /health returns 503 when Postgres or Redis is down
Endpoint is publicly accessible (no auth required)

tickets.title: Set up ESLint, Prettier, and Husky on backend
tickets.description: Audit and extend existing eslint.config.mjs: add @typescript-eslint rules for no-explicit-any, no-unused-vars, explicit-function-return-type. Configure Prettier. Add Husky + lint-staged: run eslint --fix and prettier --write on staged .ts files before commit.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm lint passes with zero errors on the current codebase
pnpm format formats all files consistently
git commit is blocked if lint fails
CI runs pnpm lint as a first step

tickets.title: Set up GitHub Actions CI pipeline
tickets.description: Create .github/workflows/backend-ci.yml that runs on PRs to main: steps are install → lint → unit tests → build. Use a Postgres and Redis service container so integration tests can run in CI. Set NODE_ENV=test.
acceptanceCriteria: CI pipeline runs automatically on PRs targeting main
Pipeline fails if lint, tests, or build fails
Postgres and Redis are available in the CI environment
Build artifact is produced successfully

tickets.title: Initialise frontend project structure and aliases
tickets.description: Set up the src/ folder structure as defined in the system design: components/, features/, hooks/, lib/, pages/, store/, types/, services/, router/. Configure path aliases (@/* → src/*) in vite.config.ts and tsconfig.app.json. Verify aliases resolve in IDE.
acceptanceCriteria: All directories exist
Import '@/store/sessionStore' resolves correctly
pnpm dev starts without errors
TypeScript strict mode is enabled in tsconfig.app.json

tickets.title: Configure Tailwind CSS v4 and design tokens
tickets.description: Install tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/vite. Add the plugin to vite.config.ts. Define CSS custom properties in src/index.css: --color-table (dark green), --color-card-bg (white), suit colors, active-player highlight. Configure a custom Tailwind theme that maps to these tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: A component using bg-[--color-table] renders the correct green
pnpm dev hot-reloads correctly when Tailwind classes change
Design tokens are documented in a short comment block in index.css

tickets.title: Install shadcn/ui and add core primitives
tickets.description: Initialise shadcn/ui via CLI (pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init). Add the following components: button, badge, card, dialog, toast, tooltip, skeleton, separator. Wire the Toaster into App.tsx root. Verify each component renders in isolation.
tickets.technicalNotes: The shadcn MCP tool is installed in this VS Code workspace. Use it to get the correct add commands, browse component source, and view usage examples — no need to reference external docs.
acceptanceCriteria: All 8 shadcn primitives are added under src/components/ui/
<Toaster /> is mounted in App.tsx
A test render of <Button>, <Badge>, <Dialog> all render without console errors

tickets.title: Build the Card UI primitive component
tickets.description: Create src/components/ui/PlayingCard.tsx. Props: rank (Rank), suit (Suit), faceDown (bool), selected (bool), disabled (bool), size ('sm'|'md'|'lg'), onClick. Face-up: renders rank + suit symbol with correct colour (red hearts/diamonds, black clubs/spades). Face-down: card back pattern. Selected: elevated with accent border. Accessible: aria-label='rank of suit'.
acceptanceCriteria: Face-up card shows rank and suit with correct colour
Face-down card shows a back pattern (no rank/suit visible)
selected prop adds a visually distinct border/elevation
disabled prop prevents onClick and reduces opacity
All three sizes render proportionally
aria-label is set correctly for screen readers
Component has a Vitest snapshot test

tickets.title: Set up Vitest and React Testing Library
tickets.description: Install vitest, @testing-library/react, @testing-library/user-event, @testing-library/jest-dom, jsdom. Configure vite.config.ts with test: { environment: 'jsdom', setupFiles: ['./src/test/setup.ts'] }. Create setup.ts that imports @testing-library/jest-dom. Add a trivial smoke test that passes.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm test runs Vitest and passes
A sample test using render() and screen.getByText() works correctly
jest-dom matchers (toBeInTheDocument, etc.) are available in all test files

tickets.title: Set up environment config and API service base on frontend
tickets.description: Create .env.example with VITE_API_URL and VITE_SOCKET_URL. Create src/lib/config.ts that reads and validates these. Create src/services/api.ts: an axios (or fetch) wrapper that attaches the session token (from sessionStore) to all requests via an interceptor. Handles 401 by clearing session and redirecting to /.
acceptanceCriteria: .env.example is committed; .env is gitignored
api.ts correctly includes Authorization: Bearer <token> on outgoing requests
A 401 response clears the stored token and navigates to /
Config values are type-safe (not string | undefined)

epics.title: Authentication & Session Management
epics.description: Anonymous session-based auth. Players enter a display name, receive an opaque token, and are identified by that token on all HTTP and WebSocket interactions. Session must survive page refresh.

tickets.title: Create Player entity and migration
tickets.description: Add the Player model to schema.prisma: id (UUID, auto), display_name (String, max 32), created_at (DateTime, default now). Run migration. Create PlayerService with createPlayer(displayName) and findById(id) methods.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration runs cleanly: players table exists in local DB
PlayerService.createPlayer() inserts a record and returns it
PlayerService.findById() returns null for unknown IDs (does not throw)
Unit tests cover both service methods

tickets.title: Implement POST /auth/session endpoint
tickets.description: Create AuthController with POST /auth/session. Body DTO: CreateSessionDto { displayName: string } — validated: min 2, max 32 chars, trimmed. On valid request: create Player record, generate UUID v4 token, store session in Redis (key: session:{token}, value: { playerId, displayName }, TTL: 86400s). Return { token, player: { id, displayName } }.
acceptanceCriteria: POST with valid name returns 201 with token and player object
POST with name < 2 chars returns 400 with validation message
POST with name > 32 chars returns 400
Token is stored in Redis with 24h TTL
Player record is persisted to Postgres
Integration test covers happy path + validation failures

tickets.title: Build SessionGuard and @Public() decorator
tickets.description: Create SessionGuard (CanActivate): reads Authorization: Bearer <token> header, looks up token in Redis, if valid attaches player to request.user, if not returns 401. Create @Public() custom decorator that marks an endpoint as skipping the guard. Apply SessionGuard globally in main.ts; mark /auth/session and /health as @Public().
acceptanceCriteria: A protected endpoint returns 401 when no token is provided
A protected endpoint returns 401 for an expired/unknown token
request.user is populated with { id, displayName } on valid token
@Public() endpoints are accessible without a token
Unit tests cover: missing header, invalid token, valid token, @Public() bypass

tickets.title: Implement GET /auth/me and sliding session TTL
tickets.description: Add GET /auth/me (protected): returns current player info + active matchId if in a match. Add a session refresh middleware/interceptor that extends the Redis TTL to 24h on every authenticated request (sliding window). Add DELETE /auth/session (protected): deletes the Redis key.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /auth/me returns { player, matchId: null } for a freshly authenticated player
Every authenticated request extends the Redis session TTL
DELETE /auth/session removes the token from Redis; subsequent GET /auth/me with the same token returns 401

tickets.title: Build landing page and session creation form
tickets.description: Create src/pages/LandingPage.tsx. Centered layout on a dark green background. Game title 'Shah Exchange'. Display name input (min 2, max 32, trimmed, auto-focused). 'Enter Game' button. Client-side validation: show inline error if < 2 chars. Loading state on submit disables input and button. On success: navigate to /lobby.
acceptanceCriteria: Page renders correctly with title and input
Submitting a name shorter than 2 chars shows an inline error without calling the API
Input is auto-focused on mount
Enter key submits the form
Button is disabled and shows a spinner during the API call
Successful submission navigates to /lobby

tickets.title: Implement sessionStore and localStorage persistence
tickets.description: Create src/store/sessionStore.ts (Zustand). State: { token, player, isAuthenticated, isLoading }. Actions: login(displayName) calls POST /auth/session, stores result in state AND localStorage (keys: shah_session_token, shah_player). restoreSession() reads localStorage, calls GET /auth/me to validate — on 401 clears storage. logout() clears state and storage.
acceptanceCriteria: login() populates state and localStorage on success
restoreSession() restores state without re-asking for a name on page refresh
restoreSession() silently clears storage on 401
logout() clears all state and localStorage
Unit tests cover: login success, login failure, restoreSession valid, restoreSession invalid

tickets.title: Build ProtectedRoute and wire session restore on app load
tickets.description: Create src/router/ProtectedRoute.tsx: if isLoading show <LoadingSpinner />, if !isAuthenticated redirect to / with replace. Set up the router in src/router/index.tsx with all 5 routes; wrap all non-landing routes with <ProtectedRoute>. In App.tsx, call sessionStore.restoreSession() in a useEffect on mount. Authenticated users visiting / are redirected to /lobby.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to /lobby without a session redirects to /
Navigating to / with a valid session redirects to /lobby
Page refresh on /lobby restores session and stays on /lobby (no redirect to /)
Page refresh with expired token redirects to /
LoadingSpinner is shown during the restoreSession check

epics.title: Lobby & Room Management
epics.description: Full-stack feature for creating rooms, joining by code, the waiting room UI, and starting a match. Includes real-time player list updates via WebSocket.

tickets.title: Create Match and MatchPlayer Prisma models and migration
tickets.description: Add Match and MatchPlayer models to schema.prisma. Match: id, room_code (unique, char 4), host_id (FK to Player), status (enum: LOBBY/IN_PROGRESS/FINISHED), player_count, created_at, ended_at. MatchPlayer: matchId + playerId (composite PK), seat_index, joined_at. Run migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration runs cleanly; both tables exist
Foreign key constraints are enforced (host_id → players.id, etc.)
Unique constraint on room_code works (insert duplicate → DB error)

tickets.title: Implement room code generation and MatchService.createMatch()
tickets.description: Add MatchService. Implement generateRoomCode(): produces a random 4-char uppercase code from chars A-Z, 2-9 (avoids 0,1,O,I). Retry up to 5 times on uniqueness collision. Implement createMatch(hostPlayerId): creates Match record (status: LOBBY), creates MatchPlayer for host at seat_index 0, stores initial MatchState in Redis (match:{matchId}:state), returns full MatchState.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated codes are always 4 chars and only use valid characters
Duplicate codes are retried (test with a mock that always returns the same code until the 3rd try)
Match and MatchPlayer records are written to Postgres
MatchState is stored in Redis
Unit tests cover code generation and createMatch() happy path

tickets.title: Implement POST /match and POST /match/join endpoints
tickets.description: Create MatchController. POST /match (auth required): calls MatchService.createMatch(), returns { matchId, roomCode, match: MatchState }. POST /match/join (auth required), body: { roomCode }. Validates: room exists, status is LOBBY, player count < 8, player not already in another active room. Assigns next seat_index. Updates Redis. Returns MatchState. Emit match:updated WebSocket event stub (log for now).
acceptanceCriteria: POST /match returns 201 with matchId, roomCode, and full match state
POST /match/join with valid code adds player and returns updated state
POST /match/join on non-existent code returns 404
POST /match/join on a full room (8 players) returns 409
POST /match/join on an in-progress match returns 409
Integration tests cover all error cases

tickets.title: Implement DELETE /match/:id/leave and host migration
tickets.description: Add MatchService.leaveMatch(matchId, playerId). Removes player from MatchPlayer. If player was host and others remain: assign host to the player with the lowest seat_index. If no players remain: delete the match from DB and Redis. POST /match/:id/start (auth, host only): validates player count >= 4, transitions status to IN_PROGRESS, will be fully wired in EP-005.
acceptanceCriteria: Leaving removes the player from the room
Host leaving with others present migrates host to next-seat player
Last player leaving deletes the Match and cleans Redis
Non-host calling start returns 403
Host calling start with < 4 players returns 400

tickets.title: Build lobby page (create or join room)
tickets.description: Create src/pages/LobbyPage.tsx. Two cards side by side: 'Create Room' (button → calls POST /match) and 'Join Room' (4-char code input + button → calls POST /match/join). Code input auto-uppercases, limits to 4 chars. Error states: 'Room not found', 'Room is full', 'Game already started'. Loading states on buttons. On success: navigate to /room/:code.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Room calls API and navigates to /room/:code on success
Join Room's input auto-uppercases and limits to 4 chars
Joining a non-existent code shows inline 'Room not found' error
Joining a full room shows 'Room is full' error
Buttons are disabled during API calls
Player's display name is visible in the page header

tickets.title: Build waiting room page with player list and seat grid
tickets.description: Create src/pages/WaitingRoomPage.tsx. Fetches GET /match/:id on mount. Displays: room code with copy button, player seat grid (4–8 slots, filled/empty), player count, host crown badge, 'Start Game' button (host only, enabled when >= 4 players), 'Waiting for host...' for non-hosts, Leave Room button.
acceptanceCriteria: Room code is displayed and copyable to clipboard
Seat grid renders correct number of slots based on current player count
Host player has a visible host badge
Start Game is only visible to the host
Start Game is disabled when < 4 players are present
Leave Room navigates back to /lobby

tickets.title: Build matchStore and wire real-time lobby WebSocket events
tickets.description: Create src/store/matchStore.ts (Zustand): { matchId, roomCode, hostPlayerId, players, status }. Wire socket events in the waiting room: match:updated → updatePlayers(), match:host_changed → setHost(), game:started → navigate to /game/:matchId. Connect socket when the WaitingRoomPage mounts; disconnect on unmount. (Socket client singleton from T-058 can be stubbed here.)
acceptanceCriteria: matchStore updates correctly when match:updated is received
Host badge updates when match:host_changed is received
All players in the room see the updated player list when someone joins
game:started event navigates all players to /game/:matchId
Unit tests cover store actions

epics.title: Core Game Engine
epics.description: Pure, stateless, server-side game rule engine. No I/O. Takes a GameState + intent, returns new GameState + event list. Shared types are defined here and mirrored to the frontend. This is the most test-critical module in the project.

tickets.title: Define all shared TypeScript types
tickets.description: Create src/shared/types/: card.types.ts (Card, Rank, Suit, SetSize), game-state.types.ts (Player, Pile, Play, RoundState, GameState, MatchState, Direction, GameStatus, MatchStatus), events.types.ts (PlayIntent, EngineResult, GameEventType, ExchangeAction). All types must be exported. No logic — types only.
acceptanceCriteria: All types from SYSTEM_DESIGN.md §5 are defined
Types compile cleanly with zero errors
No circular dependencies between type files
Types are importable from '@/shared/types'

tickets.title: Implement DeckService: buildDeck and shuffleDeck
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/deck.service.ts. buildDeck(): returns all 52 cards (4 suits × 13 ranks). shuffleDeck(deck, seed?): Fisher-Yates shuffle, pure function. Both must be pure (no side effects). Include seeded shuffle variant for deterministic testing.
acceptanceCriteria: buildDeck() returns exactly 52 unique cards
shuffleDeck() output is a permutation of input (same cards, different order)
shuffleDeck() with the same seed produces the same result every time
Unit tests: deck length, no duplicates, shuffle is a permutation

tickets.title: Implement DeckService: dealHands
tickets.description: Add dealHands(playerCount: number, deck: Card[]): { hands: Card[][], discarded: Card[] } to DeckService. Implements the dealing table from the rules: 4→13 cards, 5→10, 6→8, 7→7, 8→6. Remaining cards are discarded. Throws for invalid player counts.
acceptanceCriteria: All 6 player counts (4–8, plus invalid) are tested
Total cards in hands + discarded always equals 52
Each hand has the correct card count for its player count
Invalid player count (e.g. 3 or 9) throws a descriptive error

tickets.title: Implement rank comparison utilities
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/rank.utils.ts. Implement: PLAY_RANK_ORDER array (3→A, excludes 2), EXCHANGE_RANK_ORDER array (3→2), comparePlayRank(a, b): number, isReset(rank): boolean (rank === '2'), getResetRequirement(pileSize): SetSize (returns how many 2s are needed to reset that pile size).
acceptanceCriteria: comparePlayRank('3', 'A') returns negative
comparePlayRank('K', 'K') returns 0
isReset('2') returns true; isReset('A') returns false
getResetRequirement(1) = 1, (2) = 1, (3) = 2, (4) = 3
Unit tests cover all cases including edge values

tickets.title: Implement RulesService: normal play validation
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/rules.service.ts. Implement validatePlay(state, intent): ValidationResult for the non-reset path: checks it is the player's turn, player has the cards in hand, all cards are the same rank, set size matches pile (if active), rank >= pile rank. Returns { valid: true } or { valid: false, reason: string }.
acceptanceCriteria: Returns invalid when cards are not in the player's hand
Returns invalid when cards have mixed ranks
Returns invalid when pile is active and set size doesn't match
Returns invalid when rank is lower than pile rank
Returns valid for same rank (skip case — just validates, does not apply skip)
Returns valid for starting a round on an empty pile
Unit tests cover all 7 invalid scenarios plus happy path

tickets.title: Implement RulesService: reset (2-card) validation
tickets.description: Extend validatePlay() for the reset path. When all played cards are rank '2': check that the set size meets the reset requirement for the current pile type (single/double → 1× 2; triple → 2× 2s; quad → 3× 2s). Playing 2s on an empty pile is allowed (starts a new round with a 2 as the pile rank — treated as a normal play since pile is empty).
acceptanceCriteria: Single 2 on single pile → valid reset
Single 2 on double pile → valid reset
Double 2 on triple pile → valid reset
Triple 2 on quad pile → valid reset
Single 2 on triple pile → invalid (insufficient 2s)
Double 2 on single pile → invalid (too many 2s — can only play 1)
Playing a 2 on empty pile → valid normal play (no reset)
Unit tests cover all reset cases

tickets.title: Implement turn advancement with direction and skip logic
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/turn.utils.ts. Implement getNextActivePlayerIndex(state, currentIndex, skipCount): number. Respects direction (clockwise = +1 mod n, counterclockwise = -1 mod n). Skips finished players. If skipCount = 1, skips one additional active player. Returns -1 only if no active players remain (guard case).
acceptanceCriteria: Clockwise: advances +1 correctly, wraps around
Counterclockwise: advances -1 correctly, wraps around
Finished players are skipped automatically
skipCount=1 skips one additional active player after the normal advance
Both directions tested with all player counts 4–8
Handles the case where only 1 active player remains

tickets.title: Implement GameEngineService.processIntent(): pass branch
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/game-engine.service.ts. Implement processIntent() for the pass case only. Increment consecutivePassCount. Advance turn (skip finished players). Check: if consecutivePassCount === activePlayers - 1 → round ends (clear pile, reset pass count, last-player-who-played becomes active). Return new state + events. Must deep-clone input state before mutating.
acceptanceCriteria: Passing increments consecutivePassCount in the returned state
Turn advances to the next active player
Round ends correctly when all others have passed
The last-play winner becomes the active player after a round-end pass sequence
Input state is NOT mutated (pure function — verify with Object.freeze in tests)
Unit tests: single pass, chain of passes leading to round end

tickets.title: Implement GameEngineService.processIntent(): normal play branch
tickets.description: Extend processIntent() for valid non-reset plays. Remove played cards from the player's hand. Update pile.topPlay. Reset consecutivePassCount to 0. Emit PILE_UPDATED event. If same rank as pile → set skip flag for next turn. Check hand empty → mark player finished, assign rank, emit PLAYER_FINISHED. Check all players finished → emit GAME_FINISHED. Advance turn.
acceptanceCriteria: Played cards are removed from the player's hand in the returned state
Pile topPlay is updated correctly
Same rank play sets the skip flag, and the following player is skipped
Player with empty hand is marked isFinished=true with correct finishRank
GAME_FINISHED is emitted when the last player finishes
processIntent() returns { error } (no state change) for invalid plays
Unit tests cover: normal beat, same-rank skip, player finish, game finish

tickets.title: Implement GameEngineService.processIntent(): reset play branch
tickets.description: Extend processIntent() for valid reset plays (rank === '2'). Remove 2-card(s) from player's hand. Set pile.topPlay = null. Do NOT advance turn (player continues). Reset consecutivePassCount to 0. Emit PILE_RESET event. Check if player hand is now empty (finish possible by playing last 2s). Return state.
acceptanceCriteria: Pile is cleared (topPlay = null) after a valid reset
Active player index does NOT change after a reset
Player can play again immediately (next processIntent call with same player is valid)
Player finishing by playing last 2s as a reset is correctly handled
Unit tests: single 2 on single pile, double 2 on triple pile, player finishes via reset

tickets.title: Implement determineDirection() utility
tickets.description: Implement determineDirection(winnerSeatIndex, secondPlaceSeatIndex, totalPlayers): Direction in turn.utils.ts. Uses circular seat geometry: if 2nd place is in the 'right half' (clockwise from winner) → 'clockwise'; if in the 'left half' → 'counterclockwise'. Tie-break (exactly opposite): defaults to 'clockwise'.
acceptanceCriteria: For 4 players: winner=0, 2nd=1 → clockwise; winner=0, 2nd=3 → counterclockwise
For 6 players: correctly handles all 5 possible 2nd-place positions relative to winner
All player counts 4–8 are tested
Directly opposite seat returns 'clockwise'

tickets.title: Write comprehensive game engine test suite
tickets.description: Write a thorough test suite in src/game-engine/__tests__/. Use a GameStateFactory helper to build valid initial states for tests. Cover all scenarios from the rules: deal correctness, all pass scenarios, all play scenarios, reset scenarios, skip scenarios, finish detection, direction determination. Target: 90%+ line coverage on the game-engine module.
acceptanceCriteria: pnpm test --coverage shows >= 90% line coverage for src/game-engine/
All scenarios listed in BE-EP-004 acceptance criteria have corresponding tests
No tests rely on other tests' state (fully isolated)
Tests run in under 5 seconds total

tickets.title: Mirror shared types to frontend
tickets.description: Create src/types/ files on the frontend mirroring the backend shared types: card.types.ts, game-state.types.ts, events.types.ts. These are manual copies (not auto-generated yet). Add a README note in the types folder explaining they must stay in sync with backend src/shared/types/.
acceptanceCriteria: All types needed by FE components are available under src/types/
Types compile cleanly on the frontend
The Card type is used in the PlayingCard component from T-011

epics.title: Real-Time Game Play
epics.description: Full-stack: WebSocket gateway, game lifecycle orchestration, game board UI, and socket integration. After this epic, the game is end-to-end playable in a browser.

tickets.title: Create Game Prisma model and migration
tickets.description: Add Game model to schema.prisma: id, match_id (FK), game_number (Int), direction (enum), status (enum), started_at, ended_at. Add GameRanking model: game_id + player_id (composite PK), rank (Int). Add GameEvent model: id (BigInt autoincrement), game_id, round_number, event_type, player_id (nullable), payload (Json), created_at. Run migration.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration runs cleanly; all three tables exist
Foreign keys and indexes are correct (index on game_events.game_id)
GameEvent.payload column is JSON type

tickets.title: Build WebSocket Gateway skeleton with authentication

acceptanceCriteria: Disconnected player's turns are auto-passed for up to 5 minutes

epics.title: Card Exchange System
epics.description: The post-game card exchange mechanic. After each game, 1st↔last exchange 2 cards and 2nd↔2nd-last exchange 1 card, using a specific value ordering where '2' is best. Covers backend algorithm and frontend visualization.

tickets.title: Implement ExchangeService: best and worst card selection
tickets.description: Create src/game-engine/exchange.service.ts. Implement getWorstCards(hand, count): returns the N lowest-value cards by exchange ranking (3 is worst). Implement getBestCards(hand, count): returns the N highest-value cards (2 is best). For ties in rank, use suit as a tiebreaker (hearts > diamonds > clubs > spades) for determinism.
acceptanceCriteria: getWorstCards([K♠, 3♥, 7♦], 1) returns [3♥]
getBestCards([K♠, 2♣, A♦], 1) returns [2♣] (2 is highest)
Tiebreaker by suit is deterministic
Both functions handle requesting more cards than exist in hand gracefully (return all available)
Unit tests cover: hands with 2s, hands without 2s, exact card count requests, suit tiebreakers

tickets.title: Implement ExchangeService.computeExchange()
tickets.description: Implement computeExchange(rankedPlayers: Player[]): ExchangeResult. Determines exchange pairs (1st↔last, 2nd↔2nd-last). Calls getWorstCards and getBestCards for each side. Builds ExchangeAction list. Returns both the actions and updatedHands Map<playerId, Card[]>. Must handle all player counts 4–8. Cards are matched on both rank AND suit when removing from hands.
acceptanceCriteria: 1st place gives 2 worst cards and receives 2 best cards from last
2nd place gives 1 worst card and receives 1 best card from 2nd-last
Total cards per player is unchanged after exchange (no cards lost or duplicated)
Works correctly for all player counts 4–8
Unit tests: 4 players, 6 players, 8 players; hands with multiple 2s; edge case where both exchange partners have the same best card rank

tickets.title: Integrate exchange into game-finished flow and emit game:exchange
tickets.description: In GameService.handleGameFinished(): after persisting rankings, call ExchangeService.computeExchange(). Apply updated hands to player objects. Store as the initial hand state for the next game. Build ExchangeSummary DTO and emit game:exchange to the match room. Cards given away by each player are visible to all; updated hands are sent privately per player in the next game:started event.
acceptanceCriteria: game:exchange is emitted after every game (except the last game of a match)
ExchangeSummary contains correct giver, receiver, and card details for each pair
Updated hands are correctly applied when the next game is dealt
Each player's updated hand is private (not exposed in the broadcast exchange payload)
